I've mulled this over since seeing this and have mixed-positive feelings about this.

Pros:

  • It seems they're taking controller and DLC support very seriously. Considering that backwards compatibility was one of the areas where RB4 on console really shined I have confidence that Harmonix will pull this off to the best of their ability and it seems that they're putting as much support as possible behind the PC port to ensure parity with consoles. Not having to buy more instruments or being able to score old, cheap instruments thrifting is a very nice selling point, especially for those of us who already bought RB4 on PS4/XB1.

  • RBN returning. This one is huge since it ensures a steady stream of new songs as long as people are interested in making them for RB4 (and judging by the customs scene that sprung up between RB3 and 4 and the customs scene from Rocksmith, I'd say that interest is quite high). It also provides a good example of how paid modding can work well if Harmonix handles it right in regards to quality control and IP management. Finally, it's curated like the existing paid workshops (CS:GO, DOTA 2, etc.) rather than being a free-for-all like Skyrim's was, so most of the problems Skyrim had will hopefully be minimized.

  • Not having gameplay recording blocked will be nice. I get why they blocked it on console since music licensing is a bitch, but being able to save a video in OBS if I FC a song will be nice.

  • Sumo Digital seems to be a competent developer for PC, based on their admittedly small portfolio.

Neutral:

  • Crowdfunding. Yeah, the argument can be made that they're a AA developer and that they should take the risk themselves. And crowdfunding puts a lot of people off due to past failures, as any fan (likely ex-fan now) of Peter Moleynuex or Tim Schefer can attest (speaking of Schefer, why the hell are they citing Broken Age as a crowdfunding success in their campaign? It's not doing them any favors.) At the same time, the argument can be made that Harmonix remaining independent and seeking crowdfunding is a far better proposal than seeking a publisher or investor that might try and meddle in the development (demanding strict DRM, shutting down any unofficial modding scene that pops up, etc.) Not to mention that it seems that just making RB4 for console was a huge risk in itself and now they want to port to a nearly untested market. I can't really fault them for going this route, but a 50/50 split with Harmonix and funders putting up equal risk would've gone over a lot better with me. If the alternative is RB4PC not existing, I prefer the crowdfunding.

  • Potential external mod support. I can't imagine that Harmonix will outright condone an external modding scene, but so far they've been content to simply ignore it with an unwritten rule that anything that is released officially is off limits. If they keep their current stance of turning a blind eye to it, it'll flourish with the ease of modding on PC and add serious value to the game (especially for current console owners who can just grab the game on sale for mods and RBN). However, I do fear that the ease of modding PC will make it popular enough that they'll shut it down (or more likely be pressured to shut it down by their music partners under threat of not allowing DLC to be released on PC). They did block customs in the past through updates on the 360, so I'm afraid the same will come to pass on PC; Rock Band customs are already in a precarious position and this could tip it over the edge permanently. This is the only thing that I've seen them say about it and it doesn't say anything about if they'll prevent the distribution of the files for "audition" mode.

If the modding scene develops properly and the RBN takes off, this could be great for existing owners to get access to more songs (plus not to mention the PC's RBN being a testing ground for future console DLC) on top of bringing it to a new platform. I probably will get it after release due to my laptop being portable and more convenient than my PS4 and then still have my old song library on the PS4. The main thing putting me off is that it's on Fig and not Kickstarter or Indiegogo (I know that those aren't the paragons of quality control, but they're a lot more tested than Fig).
